DataSource.description:
Provenance of a dataset artifact.

Surfaced in the API and the frontend. The spec forbids presenting
synthetic or augmented data as observed behaviour, so provenance is a
first-class field rather than a documentation footnote.
DataSource.title: DataSource

EventIngest.description:
One behavioural event submitted to the API.

Accepted events advance the online feature state through the same
``apply_event`` the offline scan uses, so serving stays consistent with
training rather than drifting between them.
EventIngest.title: EventIngest

ModelStatus.description: One loaded model's identity and provenance.
ModelStatus.title: ModelStatus

PipelineTraceResponse.description:
Which items each stage of the pipeline held, for one request.

A diagnostic, served from its own endpoint rather than bolted onto every
recommendation response: it is two orders of magnitude larger than the
result it explains, and the serving path has no use for it.

Requesting a trace forces a full pipeline run and bypasses the cache,
because a cached response has no stage membership to report and
reconstructing one from the final list would describe a funnel that never
ran.

candidate_ids.title: Candidate Ids

candidate_sources.description: Item ids proposed by each source. An item appears under every source that returned it, so the overlap between sources is visible.
candidate_sources.title: Candidate Sources

final_ids.description: What the business rerank actually returned.
final_ids.title: Final Ids

ranked_ids.description: Candidates in ranker order, best first.
ranked_ids.title: Ranked Ids

ranked_scores.description: Ranker output per entry in ranked_ids. An ordinal utility, not a probability.
ranked_scores.title: Ranked Scores

ReadinessResponse.description:
Readiness, with per-dependency detail.

A bare boolean is not actionable during an incident: what matters is
*which* dependency is down, so each is reported separately.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

business_adjustment.description: Sum of deterministic policy adjustments. Kept separate from the model score so any ranking change is attributable.
business_adjustment.title: Business Adjustment

ml_relevance_score.description: The ranking model's output. An ordinal utility from LambdaRank, NOT a calibrated probability - do not read it as one.
ml_relevance_score.title: Ml Relevance Score

sources.description: Retrieval sources that proposed this item.
sources.title: Sources

RecommendationExplanation.description:
Why one item was ranked where it was.

Values are exact TreeSHAP contributions from the ranking model, signed:
negative means the feature pushed this item *down*. They are the model's
real attributions for this specific score, not a narrative written after
the fact.
RecommendationExplanation.title: RecommendationExplanation

StageLatency.description:
Milliseconds spent in each stage of the request.

Returned on every response so a slow request is diagnosable from the
response alone. The fields mirror the pipeline stages exactly, which is
what lets the frontend's Pipeline Inspector show real numbers rather than
a drawing.
StageLatency.title: StageLatency

info.description:
Multi-stage recommendation and personalization API.

**Data provenance:** behavioural events come from the Retailrocket dataset (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Merchants, regions, prices and verticals are synthesised - see `docs/data-card.md`. Nothing here is real production traffic.
info.title: MercuryRec

get.description:
Return item coordinates for the galaxy.

Args:
    method: ``umap`` (structure-preserving, approximate for new points) or
        ``pca`` (linear, so a user vector projects in exactly).
    max_items: Point budget. The scene stops being *readable* before it
        stops being fast, so this is a legibility limit as much as a
        performance one.
    vertical: Restrict to one vertical.
    preset: Dataset preset.

schema.title: Response Projection Api V1 Embeddings Projection Get

get.description:
Describe the available projections and their limitations.

Served separately so the UI can label which method is active and, for
UMAP, state plainly that the user star is a similarity-weighted barycentre
rather than an exact projection.

schema.title: Response Projection Meta Api V1 Embeddings Projection Meta Get

get.description:
Return where a user sits among the projected items.

Two genuinely different placements, and the response says which one it
gave:

- **PCA** is a linear map, so the user's embedding projects in *exactly*,
  through the same basis and the same unit-sphere normalisation the items
  went through. ``is_exact`` is true.
- **UMAP** is non-parametric and has no transform for an unseen point. The
  star is placed at a softmax-weighted barycentre of the user's nearest
  projected items, which is an approximation. ``is_exact`` is false.

Collapsing the two into one unlabelled number would present an estimate
with the same authority as a measurement.

schema.title: Response User Position Api V1 Embeddings User  User Id  Get

get.summary: Place one user in the projection

post.description:
Accept events, advance the online feature state, invalidate caches.

Events are folded in through the same ``apply_event`` the offline scan
uses, so online state evolves exactly as training would have evolved it.
Unknown users are rejected rather than silently dropped, and the count is
returned: a client sending ids the service cannot resolve should find out.

get.description:
Expose the knobs that shape a recommendation.

Deliberately excludes every connection string and credential: this
endpoint is reachable by the browser.

schema.title: Response Config Insights Api V1 Insights Config Get

get.description:
Live counts from the loaded dataset, with provenance attached.

Provenance travels with the numbers deliberately: a consumer must be able
to tell that behaviour is real Retailrocket while merchants, regions and
prices are synthesised, without reading the docs.

schema.title: Response Dataset Insights Api V1 Insights Dataset Get

get.description:
Serve the committed drift report.

Read from an artifact rather than computed per request: comparing two
quarter-million-row windows takes seconds and allocates hundreds of
megabytes, which is not something an interactive dashboard should trigger
on every page load.

schema.title: Response Drift Insights Api V1 Insights Drift Get

get.description:
Return the committed model comparison.

Read from ``artifacts/evaluation/<preset>/results_test.json``, which is
written by ``mercury train baselines``. If it is absent this returns 404
with the command that produces it, rather than inventing plausible
numbers to fill the dashboard.

schema.title: Response Evaluation Insights Api V1 Insights Evaluation Get

get.description:
Return the offline A/B comparison and the promotion gate result.

The payload carries is_simulated and a disclaimer describing exactly what
the comparison establishes, so the frontend can render it behind a warning
badge rather than as an online experiment result.

schema.title: Response Experiment Insights Api V1 Insights Experiment Get

get.summary: Offline A/B simulation and gate verdict

get.description:
Summarise this process's own observed latency and cache behaviour.

Percentiles are computed from the Prometheus histogram buckets this
process has actually recorded. **When no requests have been served the
response says so** instead of reporting zeros that would read as
measurements.

schema.title: Response Metrics Summary Api V1 Insights Metrics Summary Get

get.description: Return the staged pipeline comparison and the retrieval ceiling.

schema.title: Response Ranking Insights Api V1 Insights Ranking Get

get.description:
Return a spread of real user ids, with how much history each one has.

Without this the explorer asks for a user id the visitor has no way to
know, and the only reachable path through the product is the cold-start
one. The ids are drawn across the history distribution rather than from
its head, because a demo that only ever shows the most active user in the
dataset is showing the easiest case and calling it typical.

Sorted deterministically, so a reload does not reshuffle the list.

schema.title: Response Sample Users Api V1 Insights Sample Users Get

get.summary: Real user ids to explore with

get.description: Nearest neighbours by item-item collaborative similarity.
get.summary: Items similar to a given item

Return ranked, re-ranked recommendations for one user.

Context parameters are optional; supplying them changes the result, which
is what makes contextual personalisation demonstrable rather than claimed.

get.description:
Return which items each stage held, for the pipeline and galaxy views.

Counts alone say 600 candidates became 10 recommendations. Only the
membership says *which* 600, which is the difference between a diagram of
a funnel and a picture of one that ran.

post.description:
Recommend from in-session behaviour.

``user_id`` may be omitted: an anonymous session is served through the
cold-start path rather than rejected, because an anonymous visitor is the
most common request a live system receives.

get.description:
Report that the process is alive.

Deliberately checks nothing external.
Expose metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format.

Report whether this instance can serve, dependency by dependency.

Returns 503 when not ready so a load balancer removes the instance
without needing to parse the body.
